storylines.title: Tyrese Haliburton Says Achilles '100 Percent' With No Restrictions
storylines.summary: Tyrese Haliburton said Monday he is "100 percent" healthy and will have no restrictions for the 2026-27 NBA season. "I am healthy," said Haliburton. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I'm good. I'm ready to go for the year. "Now that we have guys coming back and I've been able to play in pickup and stuff, I'll be just fine. Don't worry." Haliburton missed all of the 2025-26 season after tearing his Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Indiana Pacers were one win from its first championship when the injury happened. Without him, the Pacers went 19-63, the league's second-worst record. They also lost their first-round pick in a midseason trade with the LA Clippers for center Ivica Zubac. Rick Carlisle pointed to the impact of his absence. "You don't realize how important one player can be until you are without that player for a significant period of time," said Carlisle. Haliburton said the team cannot ignore last season as it tries to rebound. "We can watch as much film as we want from two years ago and the way our offense and defense looked, but we can't pretend like last year didn't happen," said Haliburton, who also battled shingles during his recovery. "We've got to correct those things to go into this year." The Eastern Conference looks different since the Finals. The New York Knicks won their first title in 53 years, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joined the Philadelphia 76ers, and Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to the Miami Heat. Carlisle said the team has not set a minutes plan for Haliburton ahead of the Oct. 21 opener against the New Orleans Pelicans. "I can't tell you exactly what the load is going to be," said Carlisle. "We will be in very animated communication about it with the training staff and with him. At this point, it really appears that he has made a great recovery and a great return to play."

storylines.title: LeBron James confirms he nearly joined the Knicks, will live part-time in New York while playing for 76ers
storylines.summary: James, who made his public debut in a 76ers jersey on Monday, likely would have signed with the Knicks if they hadn't won it all in June

storylines.title: LeBron James Says He Planned To Join Knicks Before Their Title Run
storylines.summary: LeBron James revealed he planned to sign with the New York Knicks before they won the NBA championship in June, ending a 53-year title drought. James spoke to ESPN on Monday during the Philadelphia 76ers' annual media day. James said his final decision came down to five teams in the 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves. The Knicks did not make that list, but he had envisioned finishing his career in New York. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," said James. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James said the potential backlash from joining a newly crowned champion made the idea a nonstarter. "Y'all wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all," said James, referring to the media at large. "But much respect to the Knicks, obviously. An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out [Jalen Brunson]. I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at, and I'm looking forward to it." The Knicks swept the 76ers in the second round in May, winning by an average of 22.3 points per game. James will play at the Garden twice in the regular season, on opening night Oct. 20 and again Feb. 27. James said he plans to split his time between New York and Philadelphia. "Both," said James. "Multiple residences."
